newsitem.title: USA: Epitope says unit to recall strawberries.
newsitem.headline: Epitope says unit to recall strawberries.

text.p: Epitope Inc. said Wednesday its Andrew & Williamson Sales Co. unit began a voluntary recall of frozen, sliced strawberries that may have caused an outbreak of Hepatitis A in some Michigan schools.
The Beaverton, Ore.-based company said the strawberries were sent to distributors for institutional use in six states.

The unit will recall 13 lots of strawberries that were shipped early in December, shortly before Epitope acquired Andrew & Williamson, it said. The berries were grown in Mexico and processed in San Diego, Epitope said.

"The health and well-being of the public is A&W's foremost concern," Epitope Chief Executive Adolph Ferro said. "While it is not certain that the lots being recalled are contaminated, we want to eliminate all possible risk to consumers."
He said customers had been notified and the company was cooperating with the Centres for Disease Control and Prevention and the Food and Drug Administration.
Epitope's stock fell $1.50 to $8.625 early on Nasdaq.
